problem_statement: technext/v-dashboard is a Vue 3 + Vite single-page admin dashboard (Tailwind, vue-router) whose workspace shell — a fixed sidebar and top bar — wraps every routed page (Dashboard, Tables, Forms, Cards, UI Elements, Modal, Blank) and is built statically with vite build. The dashboard needs a shared 'Deployment readiness' rail that reports the workspace's release vitals (build status, checks, coverage, last deploy) as four metric tiles, and that appears consistently across the Dashboard, Tables AND Forms routes so a reviewer sees the same release-readiness signals wherever they are in the workspace. The rail must lay out its four tiles responsively so the document never overflows horizontally on mobile, and it must match the dashboard's light slate/indigo visual system. The rail also exposes a release-channel selector (Stable / Beta / Canary) with a live '#deploy-readout' that updates on every channel click to reflect the current channel (e.g. 'Canary · 8% rollout' after clicking Canary).
required_content: A shared 'Deployment readiness' rail (a new src/components/DeployRail.vue) renders on the Dashboard, Tables AND Forms routes, reporting the workspace release vitals as four metric tiles (build, checks, coverage, last deploy).
The rail's tile row wraps responsively so the whole document never overflows horizontally on mobile (documentElement scrollWidth stays within the viewport, tolerance 24px).
The rail uses the dashboard's own light slate/indigo palette (white card, indigo eyebrow and active channel pill) so it matches the surrounding workspace rather than introducing an off-brand card.
The release-channel selector exposes a live '#deploy-readout' that updates on every channel click: after clicking Canary it reads 'Canary · 8% rollout', and it starts on 'Stable · 100% rollout'.
The existing router routes, the sidebar + top-bar shell, the dashboard cards, the users table, and the forms all stay intact (no regressions).
design_constraints: Reuse the dashboard's own local assets and Tailwind styling; introduce no external or remote media (localized team/table avatars stay under public/img).

The shared rail must be a single component rendered from the dashboard shell (DashboardLayout.vue) on the whitelisted routes so its cross-page presence is consistent; do not duplicate divergent copies per page.
Keep the rail's four tiles on a wrapping row (flex-wrap) with a fluid basis so mobile never overflows; do not pin the row to a fixed pixel width.
The release-channel readout must be a reactive/computed value bound to the live selected channel, not a value snapshotted once at component setup.
state_constraints: The initial states (desktop, tablet, mobile) capture the /dashboard route with the readiness rail pinned to the top of the workspace content above the users table.

The desktop_tables and desktop_forms states capture the /tables and /forms routes where the shared rail must also be present; desktop_dashboard_canary clicks the Canary channel pill on /dashboard to update the live readout.

change_completion: The 'Deployment readiness' rail renders on the Dashboard, Tables, and Forms routes with its four metric tiles and grounded release copy.
The release-channel readout updates to 'Canary · 8% rollout' after the Canary channel is clicked, reflecting the live selection.
design_consistency: The rail matches the dashboard's light slate/indigo palette (white card, indigo eyebrow and active pill) rather than an off-brand dark card, matching the reference visually.
The rail reuses the dashboard's own Tailwind layout and the sidebar, top bar, cards, and users table stay intact.
responsive: The rail's tile row wraps on mobile so the document does not overflow horizontally beyond the 24px tolerance on mobile_initial.
The workspace shell, cards, table, and rail remain usable across desktop, tablet, and mobile viewports.
regression: The sidebar wordmark and the users table remain present so the workspace shell stays intact.
The release-channel pills still toggle the active channel and the readout still reflects the live selection.

author_notes: L4-hardened design-continuity add on technext/v-dashboard: the shared Deployment readiness rail is the vehicle for four orthogonal gates. D6 (no_horizontal_overflow) is measured on mobile_initial where the rail is present in all legs; D3 (visual_regression) compares the rail's /dashboard render against the reference over the rail component crops; D2 (dom_assertions) checks the rail's cross-page presence on the Tables and Forms routes; D4 (interaction_assertions) checks the release-channel readout updates live after clicking the Canary pill. The baseline reproduces the original layout defect (fixed-width non-wrapping tile row) and an off-brand dark-teal palette so it fails D6/D3/D2 but not D4; the bad solution is a smart-wrong rail that keeps that defect and also freezes the readout so it fails all four. Reuses the dashboard's own Tailwind assets; no remote media.

metadata.selected_repo_reason: Vue 3 + Vite Tailwind admin dashboard with a shared sidebar/top-bar shell (DashboardLayout) wrapping a multi-route SPA (Dashboard / Tables / Forms / Cards / UI Elements / Modal / Blank) — an ideal host for an L4 design-continuity task that adds a shared cross-page deployment-readiness rail (D2/D3/D6) and wires a live release-channel readout (D4).
